name: Review ergonomics and speed on a full house
summary: The row is a good spreadsheet line: it never spills sideways at 1440, 1024 or 390, the name wraps, Each × Qty = Total works, and typing a name, a count or a figure costs 10–22 ms with no redraw. Ticking, selecting, opening a record or choosing a destination is different. Each one redraws the whole desk: 21,500 elements at 600 lines, about 0.9 s per tick on this machine and 4.3 s with the CPU slowed 4x. A destination change then moves the row about ten screens away, away from the Who takes it box it now needs. Three defects break the evening review on a full house. After the first tick only 142 rows keep their photograph, so on a 600-line house three quarters show an emoji. The search box keeps only the first letter typed at a normal pace. The first figure typed over Agent Two's value drops the keyboard. Two more cost work: the record repeats the name and the recipient in boxes that fall out of step and can write an old value back, and under the Not reviewed chip the next line slides under the finger, so a double tap reviews a line nobody looked at. For the trust attorney, the worst gap: Select all plus Mark reviewed, eight presses, stamped "REVIEWED — all 48 items" on an estate schedule that listed four blank '—' lines and 24 items with no destination. A value corrected on the row prints 'not stated' with nothing on the row saying so. One tick on half of a duplicate pair silently clears the warning, and both lines print. The photographs are too small to check a count or read a mark (72 px on the row, 240 px in the record; anything bigger means going to Drive), and Agent One's 'Read:' basis never appears on screen. The plan, in order: fix the five defects (all small); stop full redraws for tick, select, open and destination; refuse Reviewed on unnamed lines and make the stamp honest. Then build one review mode for the honest look: a large photograph, every field, Enter for reviewed and next, unsure lines and the highest values first. Scripts and outputs are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/ROW/.
works_well: Typing a name, a count or an Each/Total on the row writes the line with no full render (0 renders measured) and Tab moves to the next box; _invEdit costs 13 ms at 300 lines and 22 ms at 600 (audit/ROW/editcost.txt).
Scroll position survives every full render: scrollY was unchanged across the Reviewed, select, open and destination presses (audit/ROW/perf300.txt, perf600.txt).

No horizontal overflow at 1440, 1024 or 390 (overflow 0, no row wider than its box); the headings line up with the boxes, and on a phone the headings go and each box names itself (audit/ROW/layout.txt).
Long names wrap in the row's textarea at every width; at 1440 a row is 85 px, about 10.6 lines a screen.
On a phone the selection bar is one 43 px line (5% of the screen), with Actions ▾ and Clear (audit/ROW/layout.txt).
Each × Qty = Total: a count changed carries Each across; a typed Total drops the stale Each (code at havellin.html:29552-29580).
After the fact, bulk Mark reviewed names the unsure lines, the agents' notes and the duplicate evidence it swept past (audit/ROW/review.txt).
_invRenderWhenIdle holds an agent run's redraw while a box has focus, so a finished run does not wipe a half-typed name.
Remove lines across a selection keeps every photograph and saves the manifest once.
measurements: renderInventoryTab, script time only, at 1440: 89–123 ms at 300 lines (11,084 elements, page 31,301 px) and 151–193 ms at 600 lines (21,499 elements, page 59,425 px). Five calls timed with performance.now; audit/ROW/perf300.txt, perf600.txt.

Redraw plus layout at 600 lines, 1024 px: 460–500 ms; one Reviewed tick to the next frame, 902 ms (audit/ROW/nothrottle.txt). With the CPU throttled 4x through CDP, as a rough stand-in for an older iPad: redraw plus layout 2.6–2.8 s, one tick 4.3 s, a count typed then Tab 1.6 s (audit/ROW/throttle.txt).

Full redraws per press, counted by wrapping renderInventoryTab: name 0, Qty 0, Each 0, Reviewed 1, select box 1, ▾ 1, ▴ 1, Where it goes 1. The one redraw seen after Each came from an agent run's held redraw landing (audit/ROW/perf*.txt, why.txt).
Ten clicks at one screen point under the Not reviewed chip at 1024 took 5.3 s and caused 10 full redraws, and ticked 10 different lines (audit/ROW/review.txt).
Bulk route: Select all (140 lines) plus Mark reviewed is 2 presses, 2 redraws and 162 ms; 19 of the 140 were unsure (audit/ROW/review.txt).
A destination change moved the row from y=406 to y=7,500 (9.8 screens) at 1024 with 120 lines, and 33,309 px down at 600 lines on 1440 (audit/ROW/focus.txt, perf600.txt).
Distance from the top of the tab to the first row: 1,365 px at 1440 (1.5 screens), 1,545 px at 1024 (2.0 screens), 868 px on an unnamed house (audit/ROW/above2.txt).

Row height 85 px at 1440 and 1024, 240 px average at 390; lines per screen 10.6, 9 and 3.5. The opened record is 1,084 px tall at 1440, 1,098 at 1024 and 2,872 at 390, with 36 boxes (audit/ROW/layout.txt).
Item column on a leaving group at 1024: 110 px. A 130-character name wraps to 163 px and the row is 238 px; at 1440 the column is 386 px (audit/ROW/whowidth.txt).
Tap targets at 1024: select box 14×14, Reviewed box 14×14 (its label 84×16), ▾ 30×23; the select box ends 8 px from the 72 px photo link (audit/ROW/layout.txt).
Thumbnails still painted after the first full redraw: 142 of 300 rows, and 142 of 600, with a 14,003-character 240 px JPEG data URI per photograph (audit/ROW/thumbs300.txt, thumbs600.txt).
The search box with 'harbor' typed at 400 ms a key: it searched 'h' and focus went to BODY; at 80 ms a key it searched 'harbor', then focus went to BODY (audit/ROW/search.txt).
Tab stops through one row: 9 (select box, photo link, name, Qty, Each, Total, Where it goes, Reviewed, ▾) (audit/ROW/review.txt).
Selection bar height: 74 px at 1440 (8% of the screen), 106 px at 1024 (14%), 43 px at 390 (5%) (audit/ROW/layout.txt).
verifier_note: The ROW report holds up. I reproduced every browser claim myself on the frozen copy at 3f25460. In most of my scripts (v01, v01b, v04, v07, v08, v09, v10, v20) the house was named through the real Name N shots button, with the stubbed agents running identify, room check and Agent Two. Only v02 (thumbnails) and v03 (search) seed straight onto the manifest, and they measure the cache and the search box, not anything the agents decide. Every defect and accuracy claim except one reproduced. The exception is ROW-08: ten clicks 150 ms apart at 300 lines ticked only one line. With 600 ms between clicks, or a quick double click, the next line was ticked each time, so I kept it at high. Some figures differ from the auditor's because the house sizes differ (for ROW-06 a 3.1-screen jump on 36 lines against their 9.8 on 120; for ROW-24 the first row 2,028 px down because my fixture has many duplicate groups), but each claim stands. Three proposals go against rules already written down. ROW-18 conflicts with Mark reviewed staying a flag with every line stamped. ROW-26 conflicts with a renamed line being researched (_avForceComps). ROW-09's first fix (name evidence ignores the tick) conflicts with _agDupEligible covering unreviewed lines only; its second fix (a notice or 'Compare first' on the row's tick) conflicts with nothing. Severity changes: ROW-01 from fix-now to high (the Court Inventory stays DRAFT and names the nameless lines; the false part is the REVIEWED stamp on the Estate Inventory Report, the Contents Record and the Contents List). ROW-09 from high to medium (the room check's photo evidence still covers reviewed lines). ROW-11 from high to medium (also, getThumbnails takes no size today: THUMB_PX is a constant at main-sync.gs:249, so the fix needs a backend change and a redeploy). ROW-19 from medium to low (the line comes back unreviewed, which is safe). Outside the ROW findings: the Name N shots confirm still says 'Nothing is valued and no disposition is set' (seen in v01.txt; the planner already has it). 'Estate of Estate of Walter Price' on the Court Inventory comes from the harness's seed name, not a defect.

findings.title: Reviewed can be stamped on lines with no name and no destination, and the schedules then read 'REVIEWED — all 48 items' over blank lines
findings.where: The row's Reviewed box (_renderInvRow, havellin.html:39829-39833); the bulk bar's Mark reviewed (_invBulkApply 37298 → _invStampLineReviewed 37229); invLineReviewed 37222; _invProgressStamp 30613
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/stamp.js on a 48-line probate and a 48-line Home Transition: 7 group Select all presses plus 1 Mark reviewed (8 presses) left 48 of 48 reviewed, with 24 lines undecided and 4 unnamed (Agent One's 'nothing to list' lines). The Estate Inventory Report (audit/ROW/stamp-probate.html) prints 'REVIEWED — all 48 items', then 'Not yet decided 24 items', then four rows reading '8 | — | Dining Room | 1 | as photographed | — | not stated' (also #20, #32, #44). The Contents Record prints 'REVIEWED all 48 items' beside 'This record is not yet complete … 4 photographed items not yet named'. The cause: invLineReviewed returns true on r.reviewed whatever the name, and the row draws an enabled Reviewed box on every line.
findings.tc_impact: The fastest route (Select all, Mark reviewed) makes every paper claim a complete review. Counsel then receives a schedule stamped REVIEWED with numbered lines whose description is '—', whose value is '—' and whose basis is 'not stated', plus a pile with no destination.
findings.proposal: 1) invLineReviewed answers false for a line with no name, and _invStampLineReviewed refuses one. On an unnamed line the row's Reviewed box is disabled, and Remove line sits on the row beside 'nothing to list'. Mark reviewed skips unnamed lines and says '4 have no name: type one or Remove lines'. 2) _invProgressStamp prints REVIEWED only when every line is reviewed and named and, on papers that state destinations, decided; otherwise 'Reviewed 44 of 48 · 24 without a destination'. 3) The schedules leave a nameless line out of the table and name it among the gaps above ('4 photographs not yet named'), as the Contents Record already does.
findings.vnote: I named a 24-shot probate house with the real button: 26 lines, of which 2 are 'nothing to list' (s7, s19, agentConf none). The row's Reviewed box on s7 is enabled. One Select all and one Mark reviewed (2 presses) gave 26 of 26 reviewed, with 26 undecided and 2 unnamed. The Estate Inventory Report prints 'REVIEWED — all 26 items', then 'Not yet decided 26 items'; item #8 prints as '8 — Dining Room 1 as photographed — not stated'. On the living job, the Contents Record and the Contents List both print 'REVIEWED — all 26 items' next to 'This record is not yet complete … 2 photographed items not yet named'. The Court Inventory stays honest: 'DRAFT — 2 items not yet valued', naming '#8 unnamed, #20 unnamed'. Cause: invLineReviewed (havellin.html:37222) returns true on r.reviewed whatever the name. I rated it high, not fix-now, because the filed instrument stays DRAFT and each paper names its own gaps. The false part is the REVIEWED stamp, which CLAUDE.md makes the only completeness signal ('Review gates nothing … stamped IN PROGRESS').

findings.title: After the first tick, three quarters of a full house's rows lose their photograph for the rest of the session
findings.where: _invSaveThumbCache havellin.html:28522 (INV_THUMB_CACHE_MAX 2,000,000 at 28521) evicts oldest-first from _invThumbs[jobId], the in-memory cache itself; _invEnsureThumbs 28578 marks every id _invThumbTried before asking, so an evicted photograph is never asked for again; _invThumbHTML 28650 and _invPaintThumbs 28618 paint only from that cache.
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/thumbs.js, with getThumbnails answering a 240 px JPEG of 14,003 characters for every id (the server's 'a real thumbnail is ~10KB' before base64, main-sync.gs:250). At 300 lines all 300 rows were painted after loading; after one Reviewed tick (a full redraw) 142 of 300 rows showed a photograph and the rest the category emoji, with no further getThumbnails call. At 600 lines: 142 of 600. The next session downloaded everything again (6 and 11 calls).
findings.tc_impact: On the row the photograph is the only check on Agent One's name and count; after the first tick most rows show a box or chair glyph instead. Every session also downloads every thumbnail again through Apps Script.
findings.proposal: Evict only from the persisted copy: copy the object, trim the copy, write it, and keep the session's cache whole. Better, keep thumbnails in IndexedDB or Cache Storage (not bound by the 5 MB localStorage budget the manifest needs) so they survive a reload. Ask for 120 px for the rows (fewer bytes) and the larger size only for an opened record.
findings.vnote: I stubbed getThumbnails (the action the app actually posts; the harness default answers getDriveThumbnails) to return a 14,003-character data URI per id. On a 300-line house, after load: 300 of 300 tiles painted, but the cache already held only 142 keys, with 306 ids marked tried. After one real Reviewed tick (a full redraw), 142 of 300 tiles were painted and no further getThumbnails call went out, then or 4 s later. Cause: _invSaveThumbCache (28522) deletes from _invThumbs[jobId], the in-memory object itself, and _invEnsureThumbs marks ids tried before asking. The code's own comment puts a real thumbnail at about 21 KB of base64, so the 2,000,000-character cap holds roughly 95 to 140 photographs, as-found and close-ups included.

findings.title: The desk's search box keeps only the first letter typed at a normal pace, and always loses focus
findings.where: _renderInvFilterRow havellin.html:39532 (oninput, then a 250 ms timer, then setInvQuery 37455, then renderInventoryTab, which rewrites #inv-q with innerHTML)
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/search.js at 1024 on 300 lines. 'harbor' typed at 400 ms a key: the filter held 'h', the box held 'h', focus was on BODY and 275 rows showed. Typed at 80 ms a key: the filter held 'harbor', then focus went to BODY. Browser step 44 fills the box in one go, so it never sees this.
findings.tc_impact: Finding '#31' or 'lamp' among 600 lines: typing on the iPad keyboard keeps only the first letter, the rest goes nowhere, and every refinement needs another tap on the box.
findings.proposal: Filter without rewriting the filter row: put the groups in their own host and redraw only that, or restore focus and the caret to #inv-q after the redraw. Do the same for the room picker.
findings.vnote: At 1024 px on 120 lines I typed 'harbor' with real key presses. At 400 ms a key the filter and the box both held 'h' and focus was on BODY. At 150 ms and 80 ms a key the filter held 'harbor', then focus went to BODY. Cause: oninput sets a 250 ms timer, then setInvQuery calls renderInventoryTab, which rewrites #inv-q with innerHTML and restores no focus.

findings.title: The first figure typed over Agent Two's value drops focus, so the iPad keyboard closes
findings.where: _invEdit havellin.html:29801-29804: when _wasAgentValue && ref.valuedBy !== 'agent', the row is replaced with _rowEl.outerHTML = _renderInvRow(...)
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/focus.js at 1024. A1: Total typed over an agent figure, then Tab: focus BODY. A2: Each typed, then the Where it goes box tapped: focus BODY. A3: a desk figure typed, then Tab: focus kept, on Where it goes. The comment over _invPaintFigures promises 'the box a person tapped next keeps its focus and its keyboard'.
findings.tc_impact: Most lines on a full house carry Agent Two's figure, so the first value correction on each line costs an extra tap. On the iPad the keyboard closes and reopens, and anything typed after Tab is lost.
findings.proposal: Repaint by id only what the agent figure's departure changes (the row's chip line and the record's Agent Two section), never the row. Failing that, note the focused box's column (data-cap or class) before the outerHTML and focus its twin in the new row.
findings.vnote: At 1024 px, after the real pipeline: A1, Total typed over Agent Two's $350, then Tab: focus BODY, valuedBy desk. A2, Each typed over the agent's figure, then the row's Where it goes select tapped: focus BODY. A3, a desk figure typed again on the same row, then Tab: focus kept, on Where it goes. Cause: _invEdit replaces the whole row with outerHTML when the figure stops being the agent's (havellin.html:29801-29804).

findings.title: The name and the recipient each have two boxes (row and record) that disagree after an edit, and a stale box can write the old value back
findings.where: _invPanelCols havellin.html:28464 drops seq, fmv, disposition and qty from the record because 'two inputs bound to one value is how a panel and a row silently disagree'. It does not drop objectName (the row's textarea since 2026-10-24) or channel (the row's Who takes it, _invRecipientInput 39610).
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/twice.js on a Donate line. Name typed in the record: stored 'Edited in the record', while the row's textarea still showed 'Mahogany drop-leaf side table, likely 1940s 5'. Channel typed in the record ('Habitat ReStore'): the row's box still read ''. 'Goodwill' typed in the row's box: the record still read 'Habitat ReStore'.
findings.tc_impact: One item shows two names. A correction made in one box is overwritten by the old text the next time the other box is edited. Counsel's schedule carries whichever box was typed last.
findings.proposal: Add objectName and channel to _invPanelCols' exclusions; the record keeps category, room, condition and the estate fields. Or draw the record's copy as plain text. Either way one control per value, as the comment already says.
findings.vnote: On a Donate line with its record open: the name typed in the record was stored ('Edited in the record'), while the row's textarea still showed the old name. A recipient typed in the record ('Habitat ReStore') was stored, while the row's Who box still read ''. Then a fix typed into the row's stale name box wrote the old name back (stored: 'Oil on canvas harbor scene, gilt frame, signed , walnutlower right (illegible)'), and the record's correction was lost. 'Goodwill' typed on the row was stored, while the record's box still read 'Habitat ReStore'. Cause: _invPanelCols (28464) drops seq, fmv, disposition and qty from the record, but not objectName or channel.
findings.vrepro: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-app/107e11dc-7b83-525c-829c-97f2e5cca8f9/scratchpad/audit/ROW-verify/v04.js → v04.txt (lines from 'name edited in record' on)

findings.title: Choosing where a line goes moves it about ten screens away, before its Who takes it box can be filled
findings.where: _invEdit havellin.html:29854 (a disposition change calls renderInventoryTab); _invGroupItems 37169 groups by destination first
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/focus.js C at 1024: s36 set to Distribute (To a person) moved from y=406 to y=7,500 (9.8 screens), into inv-grp-Distribute; the toast read 'Inventory workbook synced ✓'; the next row slid under the pointer. audit/ROW/perf600.txt at 1440: Donate moved the row 33,309 px down. The Who takes it box that a Sell, To a person or Donate line needs appears only on the moved row.
findings.tc_impact: Choosing Sell, then typing the auction house, means scrolling ten screens, finding the line among 25–150 others, typing, and scrolling back to where she was. Otherwise she must remember to do every recipient later, group by group.
findings.proposal: Leave a changed row where it is until the next filter or chip press (or a 'Tidy' press). Repaint it in place by id with its new destination, its Who takes it box for a leaving destination, and a quiet '→ moves to Donate' (_invSplitRepaint already repaints by id). Groups recompute on the next full redraw. Alternatively offer a room-first view for the evening pass, so a destination change never regroups.
findings.vnote: On a 36-line house at 1024 px, s2 set to Distribute through the row's own picker jumped from y=3,417 to y=5,830 (3.1 screens) into inv-grp-Distribute, and its Who takes it box exists only on the moved row. On larger houses the jump grows with the group sizes; the auditor saw 9.8 screens on 120 lines. Today's behaviour is deliberate: _invEdit's comment at 29852 says a row left where it was 'is how the list stops describing the estate', and CLAUDE.md says the desk is grouped by disposition, then room. The proposal (leave the row in place until the next filter press, repainted by id) is not on the Decided list and conflicts with no rule. Its alternative, a room-first view, would change the grouping rule and would need Anthony.

findings.title: Every tick, selection, ▾ and destination change redraws the whole desk: about a second per press at 600 lines, several seconds on a slower iPad
findings.where: _invSetReviewed havellin.html:37258-37271, _invTogglePick 37279, _invPickGroup 37284, _invToggleOpen 37461 and _invEdit 29854 (destination, room) all call renderInventoryTab 40190, which rewrites the tab with innerHTML
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/perf*.txt: renderInventoryTab takes 89–123 ms of script at 300 lines (11,084 elements) and 151–193 ms at 600 (21,499 elements). audit/ROW/nothrottle.txt, 1024 px, 600 lines: redraw plus layout 460–500 ms; one Reviewed tick 902 ms to the next frame. audit/ROW/throttle.txt, CPU throttled 4x (a rough stand-in for an older iPad): redraw plus layout 2.6–2.8 s, one tick 4.3 s. audit/ROW/review.txt: 10 ticks at 300 lines took 5.3 s.
findings.tc_impact: Reviewing 300–600 lines one tick at a time adds minutes of waiting, and the lag invites a second tap (ROW-08).
findings.proposal: Repaint by id: the row itself (its box and colour), its group heading (count, progress bar), the work bar's progress, the Needs-you chips and the selection bar, as _invSplitRepaint does for a split. Draw at most ~60 rows per open group, with 'Show the next 60' (or rows drawn as they scroll into view), so a full redraw costs a tenth of what it does now.
findings.vnote: I counted full renders on a 325-line house (11,773 elements) at 1024 px. Each Reviewed tick, select box, ▾, ▴ and Where it goes press caused 1 full render, taking 92 to 209 ms of render script and 400 to 793 ms from the press to the next frame (Playwright adds about 240 ms; name and Qty edits, with 0 renders, took 240 to 245 ms). With the CPU throttled 4x, one tick took 2.5 to 4.2 s. Name and Qty edits caused 0 renders.

findings.title: Under Not reviewed or Unsure, each tick slides the next line under the finger, so a double tap reviews an unseen line
findings.where: _invSetReviewed → renderInventoryTab while _invFilter.flag is 'unreviewed' or 'unsure' (the line stops matching and is dropped)
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/review.js at 1024: Not reviewed chip, then ten clicks at the first row's Reviewed box without moving. Ten different lines were ticked (s0, s12, s24 … s108), each one appearing under the pointer as the last vanished.
findings.tc_impact: A double tap, or a tap while a slow redraw lands (ROW-07), marks reviewed a line nobody looked at, and the paper's REVIEWED count includes it.
findings.proposal: In a review chip, keep a ticked row where it is, greyed with '✓ Reviewed · Undo', until the chip is pressed again or the TC scrolls past. Ignore a second press on the same spot within ~500 ms of a redraw.
findings.vnote: With the Not reviewed chip on, at one fixed point (the first row's Reviewed box) and 600 ms between clicks: each click ticked the line that had just slid under the pointer (s0, s6, s12, s18, s24, s30), and a quick double click ticked two (s36 and s42). One partial failure to reproduce: at 300 lines with 150 ms between clicks, ten clicks ticked only s0, apparently because clicks landing during the redraw were swallowed. Each ticked line vanishes from the chip's view, so a wrong tick is never seen.

findings.title: One tick on half of a same-name pair silently clears the duplicate warning, and both lines go to the paper
findings.where: _agDupEligible havellin.html:37954 (!r.reviewed); agentDuplicateGroups 38006; the row's tick _invSetReviewed 37258. The bulk Mark reviewed warns of this through _leftDup in _invBulkApply; the row's tick says nothing.
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/duptick.js: two Kitchen lines named 'White porcelain dinner plates' off different photographs. Before: 2 groups, 'possible duplicate' on #15. After ticking #3 alone: the pair's group gone, the chip on #15 gone, no notice. The Estate Inventory Report lists the plates twice.
findings.tc_impact: Reviewed, the most-pressed control, is the one that silently settles a possible double count, and the schedule counts 16 plates where there were 8. The bulk route names it; the row route does not.
findings.proposal: Name evidence ignores the tick: a same-name pair stays under Possible duplicates until Not duplicates (dupOK) or Remove settles it. Or, while a line is in a group, its Reviewed box reads 'Compare first' and scrolls to the group.
findings.vnote: Agent One gave 'White porcelain dinner plates' to s2 (#3) and s14 (#15), both in the Kitchen, through the real pipeline; the room check stub found no double. Before: a group of two, and both rows carried 'possible duplicate'. After one row tick on s2: the group was gone, the chip was gone from both rows (s14 still unreviewed), no notice or dialog appeared, and the Estate Inventory Report lists the plates twice. The bulk route names this case (_leftDup); the row's tick does not. Medium, not high: the room check's photo link (_arDupEligible) keeps reviewed lines in, so only the weaker same-name evidence is lost. On the proposal: 'name evidence ignores the tick' conflicts with the CLAUDE.md rule that name evidence covers Agent One's unreviewed lines only (_agDupEligible, havellin.html:37954, with its comment: 'flagging past that is nagging'). A notice on the row's tick, or 'Compare first' while a line is in a group, conflicts with nothing.

findings.title: A value corrected on the row reaches the estate's papers as 'not stated', and the row gives no sign
findings.where: _invEdit → _avTakeValue havellin.html:38752 (deletes valSource and valNote when the figure was the agent's); _renderInvRow's chip line; INV_WORK_FLAGS 37088 has no chip for a missing basis
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/srcafter.js: s0 at $350 'General estimate', with $600 typed in Total, became valSource '' and valNote ''. The chip line read 'Furniture · Living Room'. The Estate Inventory Report row reads '… | $600 | not stated |' and the Court Inventory row '… | not stated | $600 |'.
findings.tc_impact: The guide's Rule 2 is 'the row is the work', so every value the TC corrects there goes to counsel with no stated basis. Fixing it means ▾ (a full redraw), Valuation source, then ▴: 3 more presses per line, and nothing reminds her.
findings.proposal: After a figure is typed on an estate whose tier states values, the chip line shows 'basis not stated ▾' in bronze, which opens a small source picker in place (INV_VAL_SOURCES, repainted by id). Add a Needs-you chip 'No basis' so Select all plus the bulk bar's Set valuation source sweeps them. Ask Anthony whether a desk source ('Concierge estimate') should be written by default.
findings.vnote: s0 at $350 'General estimate', with $600 typed in Total on the row, became valuedBy desk with valSource '' and valNote ''. The chip line read 'Furniture · Living Room · possible duplicate', nothing about a basis. The Estate Inventory Report row reads '… Good $600 not stated', and the Court Inventory '… Good not stated $600'. The job's work chips are unnamed, unreviewed, unsure, undecided, noval, appr, norecip, noreceipt, firearm and hold: none for a missing basis. Dropping the agent's source is a recorded rule (_avTakeValue; CLAUDE.md: '…so the line reads not stated until the desk names one'), and the proposal keeps it, adding only a cue and a chip. Writing a desk source by default would change what the papers print, so it needs Anthony, as the proposal says.

findings.title: The desk cannot show a photograph big enough to check a count or read a mark
findings.where: _invRowPhotoHtml (72 px) and _invPhotoOpenHtml(…, 240) in _renderInvPanel; THUMB_PX 240 in apps-script/main-sync.gs:249 is the largest image the desk ever receives
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/layout.js: the row's photo is 72×72 at every width, and the record's is 240 px. Nothing larger exists in the app; every photograph is a link out to Drive in a new tab. Reasoning, not observed: a stack of 8 plates, or a maker's mark, cannot be counted or read in a 240 px JPEG.

findings.title: No one-line-at-a-time review: the honest look costs about two presses per line, and the fast route (2 presses) looks at nothing

findings.proposal: A Review mode from the work bar and from the Unsure and Not reviewed chips, one line a screen: the large photograph and its close-ups; name, count, category, condition, Each/Total and basis; where it goes and who; Agent One's 'Read:' and Agent Two's sales. findings.title: A tick made while Agent Two re-values a renamed line is accepted on the old figure, then silently undone
findings.where: _invSetReviewed havellin.html:37258 (never asks agentValueAgain or agentValueStale); _avWrite clears valReviewed when the new figure lands
findings.evidence: audit/ROW/focus.js B: a line renamed 'Restoration Hardware linen sofa' (agentValue sent) and ticked while the request ran read reviewed at the old $350. When Agent Two answered it read $1,500, unreviewed, box unticked. The work bar's value line said only 'Agent Two: 1 valued · review them below'.
findings.tc_impact: She signs off $350, the figure becomes $1,500 behind her back, and the line rejoins Not reviewed with nothing saying which line moved.
findings.proposal: While agentValueAgain(job, ref) or agentValueStale(ref) holds, disable the Reviewed box with 'being valued again'. When a re-value lands on a line that had been ticked, name it on the work bar ('#25 came back at $1,500: look again', with Show the item).
findings.vnote: I renamed s5 on the row ('Restoration Hardware …'), which sent one agentValue request; I held the answer. While it was held the Reviewed box was enabled, and a tick stamped reviewed and valReviewed on the old $350. When the answer landed: $1,500 'Auction comps', valReviewed false, the line not reviewed, the box unticked. The work bar said only 'Agent Two: 1 valued · review them below'. Low, not medium: the line comes back unreviewed (the safe outcome) and the Not reviewed chip gathers it. The cost is a look wasted and no pointer to the line that moved.

findings.title: The Evening Desk says a maker added to a name reprices it; in fact any edit does
findings.where: evening-desk-guide.html, Tonight's items ('A maker added to the name reprices it'); _agNameKey havellin.html:37947; agentValueAfterRename 38921
findings.evidence: _agNameKey only lowercases, collapses spaces and drops trailing punctuation, so any other change makes agentValueStale true. agentValueAfterRename then sends the line for research (_avForceComps), and the line comes back unreviewed (audit/ROW/focus.js B).
findings.tc_impact: A spelling fix moves the figure and reopens the tick without the TC expecting it.
findings.proposal: Say: 'Any change to a name sends the line to Agent Two again, researched; look at its value when it comes back.'
findings.vnote: The Evening Desk says 'A maker added to the name reprices it.' In fact any change counts. agentValueStale compares _agNameKey(valNameAt) with _agNameKey(objectName), and _agNameKey only lowercases, collapses spaces and drops trailing punctuation. agentValueAfterRename then re-values with _avForceComps. Most of the sentence is true; it understates the rule.

findings.title: A typo fix in a name sends the line for full research and reopens its review
findings.where: agentValueAfterRename havellin.html:38921 (_avForceComps); agentValueStale; _agNameKey 37947
findings.evidence: Code read: 'Persain' → 'Persian' counts as a new name, so a research request (web search and fetch) goes out, the figure is replaced and the tick reopened. audit/ROW/focus.js B shows a rename's re-value landing and unticking the line.
findings.tc_impact: Correcting the spelling on 30 lines sends 30 research runs, and 30 figures move after she has looked at them.
findings.proposal: Treat an edit of two characters or fewer, or one that only reorders words, as the same name for agentValueStale. Re-value at the line's own depth (agentValueMode) unless the edit adds a word (a maker, a model).
findings.decided_conflict: CLAUDE.md, Agent Two: 'A name changed is valued again by itself (agentValueAfterRename from _invEdit …): researched (_avForceComps)'.
findings.vnote: The behaviour is as described: any name change on an agent-valued line makes it stale, research is forced and the review reopens (_invEdit deletes valReviewed, 29770-29772). The proposal (treat small edits as the same name, and re-value at the line's own depth) goes against CLAUDE.md, Integrations, Agent Two: 'A name changed is valued again by itself (agentValueAfterRename from _invEdit …): researched (_avForceComps)' (Anthony's Restoration Hardware mirror).
